subject.title: [Security] Session hijacking vulnerability due to predictable sequence IDs in gateway client

question: Does the gateway security owner confirm that predictable per-socket event sequence numbers cannot authenticate, authorize, correlate, or inject client requests, so this public report can close as unsupported?
rationale: Source inspection strongly rejects the claimed mechanism, but the protected security labels require a human security-boundary decision and allow for private exploit evidence not present in the public issue.

options.title: Confirm unsupported and close
options.body: Confirm that `seq` is ordering-only metadata and close the public issue while inviting any materially different proof through a private GitHub Security Advisory.

options.title: Request private exploit proof
options.body: Keep the issue open temporarily and ask the reporter to privately demonstrate an unauthenticated or cross-authorization request accepted because of a guessed sequence number.

recommendation.title: Confirm unsupported and close
recommendation.body: Confirm that `seq` is ordering-only metadata and close the public issue while inviting any materially different proof through a private GitHub Security Advisory.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor guide lists Gateway and Security in this owner's area, and their merged history includes authentication-scope work in the affected handler.
